# Reading: noticing gaps during study

This is an original, synthetic classroom passage, not a published study.

## Main claim

Trying to recall an idea without looking at the notes can reveal gaps that rereading alone may hide. Feedback matters: learners need to compare an attempted answer with the source before keeping it.

## Classroom illustration

A teacher observed two existing study groups. Each group had five learners. Both groups studied the same ten definitions for fifteen minutes. Group A reread the definitions; Group B attempted recall and then checked the definitions. An immediate ten-question quiz followed.

| Group | Study activity | Average correct answers out of 10 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Rereading | 6 |
| B | Recall followed by checking | 8 |

## Limits

The groups were not randomly assigned. This was one small classroom observation, and there was no delayed test. It does not establish that the activity caused the difference, nor that the difference persists over time. The passage does not identify an author, publication date or external references.

## Practical suggestion in the passage

After studying, attempt a short explanation from memory, check it against the notes, and revise any mistakes.
